stories.headline: 40+ cybersecurity leaders urge Trump to restore Anthropic Mythos 5 and Fable 5 access

key_facts.fact: Prominent cybersecurity leaders, including CISOs and executives at Adobe, Zoom and Sophos, are urging the Trump administration to reverse restrictions on Anthropic's most advanced AI models.
The loosely organized group, led by former Facebook CSO Alex Stamos, argues in the letter that the issue Amazon researchers flagged exists across other leading AI models too.

As of Sunday evening, the letter had over 40 signatories, including Luta Security CEO Katie Moussouris, SocialProof Security CEO Rachel Tobac, Veracode co-founder Chris Wysopal, computer scientist Paul Vixie, Sophos CEO Joe Levy and Nvidia security researcher Aaron Grattafiori.
The letter argues the action 'has taken the best models away from defenders, created market uncertainty, and risked America's AI leadership without any real risk to justify it.'

Stamos, now chief product officer at Corridor, told Axios that the Fable 5 capability that alarmed the White House was the model's ability to create a 'proof of concept' for vulnerabilities; only Mythos 5 and Mythos Preview, available to Project Glasswing members, could turn those into fully autonomous attack chains.

stories.headline: Anthropic flies senior staff to DC to repair Mythos 5 and Fable 5 export-control dispute with White House

key_facts.fact: Senior technical staff from Anthropic are in Washington to meet with White House officials and try to resolve the dispute that took the company's Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models offline.
A Trump administration official tells Fox Business the export controls were triggered by Anthropic's 'recklessness' in responding to issues with its latest release.
Officials say Amazon AI experts orchestrated a jailbreak on Fable 5 after its June 9 release, opening the full cyber abilities of Mythos 5, the more advanced model in the family.

A source close to Anthropic says the initial government call gave no technical details, only a request to pull Fable 5 within 90 minutes, and that CEO Dario Amodei has been engaged from the beginning and remains eager to resolve any concerns.

A Fortune report on June 14 says Amazon CEO Andy Jassy's warning to the White House, plus concerns about unauthorized Chinese access and cybersecurity fears, led the administration to cut off foreign access to Fable 5.

stories.headline: Apple's new Siri AI 'good enough' to ease its AI crisis; iOS 27 builds include third-party AI model support beyond OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Mark Gurman, in a Power On column published June 14, writes that Apple's new Siri AI, while mainly delivering the basics, is 'good enough' to pull Apple out of its AI crisis.
Sources tell Gurman that the ability to tap third-party AI models beyond OpenAI's is already active in internal iOS 27 builds.
Gurman frames the user-facing tradeoff as 'Siri AI is like iMovie and ChatGPT is like Final Cut Pro' — Siri AI can handle the basics, but power users will want third-party AI for extra functionality.

Gurman writes that 'the new Siri finally works as it is supposed to for the first time in 15 years' and that its pre-installed status will give Apple a competitive baseline to ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude.
Gurman expects Apple to eventually build its own 'OpenClaw competitor' that could fully operate its software across iPhones, iPads and Macs on behalf of the user.
The Verge notes the new Siri is built on Gemini models, which is consistent with Apple's reported partnership with Google for Siri AI infrastructure.

stories.headline: ByteDance in talks for at least 50,000 Iluvatar CoreX inference chips, also weighing Baidu's Kunlunxin

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is in talks with Shanghai-based Iluvatar CoreX to purchase AI chips for inference work and is also considering a similar deal with Baidu, according to two sources familiar with the matter.
Iluvatar CoreX is expected to ship at least 50,000 chips to ByteDance this year, most of them for inference workloads as ByteDance widens the user base of Doubao, its consumer chatbot.
If a deal is reached, Iluvatar CoreX would become ByteDance's third major domestic GPU supplier after Huawei and Cambricon; a Baidu Kunlunxin deal would make it a fourth.
Iluvatar's flagship TianGai-100 line is positioned as a domestic alternative to Nvidia's A100; until recently the company sold almost entirely to government buyers.

ByteDance has also been developing its own custom AI silicon and was reportedly in talks with Samsung as recently as February 2026 about potential manufacturing partnerships, giving it three parallel tracks.

stories.headline: ByteDance in talks to buy 50,000+ Iluvatar CoreX AI chips, eyes Baidu Kunlunxin deal

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is in talks with Shanghai-based Iluvatar CoreX to purchase AI chips for inference work, and is also considering a similar deal for Baidu's Kunlunxin chips.
Iluvatar CoreX is expected to ship at least 50,000 chips to ByteDance this year, mostly for inference workloads supporting ByteDance's Doubao AI chatbot.
If a deal is agreed, Iluvatar CoreX would become ByteDance's third major domestic GPU supplier after Huawei and Cambricon.
Tencent is already a Kunlunxin customer; ByteDance, Iluvatar CoreX, Baidu and Tencent did not respond to requests for comment.
Iluvatar CoreX, which listed in Hong Kong in January 2026, reported 2025 revenue with about 90% coming from selling GPUs; its Tiangai chips target AI training while Zhikai chips target inference.
Iluvatar CoreX's chip shipments are projected to grow over 30% to more than 100,000 chips this year, according to a Huatai Securities research note.
ByteDance has also been developing its own custom AI silicon and was reportedly in talks with Samsung as recently as February 2026 about potential manufacturing partnerships.

stories.headline: Canadian PM Carney and EU warn US Anthropic ban shows risks of AI over-reliance and lack of tech sovereignty

key_facts.fact: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the US Anthropic ban shows the dangers of 'over-reliance on certain models', and compared the risks to those that led to the 2008 financial crisis.
The European Commission says it is looking at the practical consequences of US restrictions on Anthropic's models, noting such measures 'should not be discriminatory against partners'.
EU officials called the Anthropic decision a 'further illustration' of why Europe needs stronger tech sovereignty.

Former Trump administration AI advisor Dean Ball called the move 'baffling', pointing to inconsistency between loosening chip export controls to China and a blanket restriction on access to Anthropic models for all foreign governments, including close allies that had been relying on Mythos to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities in critical systems.

stories.headline: Tencent-backed Enflame wins STAR Market IPO approval to raise ~$830M as last of China's four leading AI chipmakers

key_facts.fact: Shanghai Enflame Technology Co., backed by Tencent, has received approval for an initial public offering on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's STAR Market, becoming the last of China's four leading AI chipmakers to go to market.
Enflame is targeting a raise of approximately RMB 6 billion (~$830 million) on the STAR Market.
Tencent holds 20.26% of Enflame and accounted for 71.84% of its revenue, making it both the company's largest shareholder and dominant customer.
Enflame, founded in March 2018, has self-iterated four generations of architecture and five cloud AI chips, with cumulative losses of RMB 4.29 billion (~$600M) over three years.
IPO proceeds are earmarked for fifth- and sixth-generation AI chip products, expected to debut in 2027 and 2029, rather than expansion of current deployments.
Chinese regulators eased listing rules for unprofitable hardware companies in June 2025, and rivals Moore Threads, MetaX and Biren have already gone public and are trading above IPO prices.

stories.headline: IQE and Tower Semiconductor sign multi-year InP epiwafer deal for AI data center optical connectivity

key_facts.fact: On June 15, 2026, IQE plc and Tower Semiconductor announced a multi-year agreement for the supply of Indium Phosphide (InP) epiwafers for optical connectivity solutions serving AI-driven data center infrastructure.

IQE's InP epiwafers will be used in several of Tower's advanced silicon photonics platforms, including technology for 200Gbs/lane pluggable transceivers and prototyping of next-generation 400Gb/lane modulators, as well as optical-circuit-switches for datacenter deployment.
The agreement provides for a minimum purchase commitment by Tower in the first year, a reciprocal supply commitment from IQE, and minimum volume commitments thereafter.

Under a separate agreement, Tower granted IQE a broad worldwide royalty-free license to porous silicon patents that had been the subject of an IP dispute, settling all litigation between the companies.

stories.headline: Brent crude plunges below $83 to three-month low as Iran deal triggers risk-off oil unwind

key_facts.fact: Brent crude tumbled 4.5% to $83.41 per barrel and WTI fell 5.5% to $80.28 on Monday June 15, both reaching their lowest levels since March 10, after the US-Iran deal announcement triggered the unwind of the conflict-era risk premium
Crude had surged to roughly $120 per barrel at the height of tensions in May and over $140 at the Strait of Hormuz closure peak in April, making Monday's settlement around $83 a dramatic retreat

European oil majors fell sharply on the news: Shell -4.5%, Equinor -5.9%, TotalEnergies -5%, Repsol -3.5%; gold rose 2.3% to $4,317/oz and US stock futures spiked, with Russell 2000 futures opening at a record high

Energy analyst Saul Kavonic told the Financial Times that oil markets were likely to remain tight through 2027 because of the time needed to restore shipping networks, repair damaged infrastructure and rebuild depleted inventories, with about 500 ships still stuck in the strait

GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan said US gas prices could fall to $3.75 a gallon by July 4 if Hormuz reopens as planned, after consumer prices rose 4.2% year-over-year in May — the highest jump since 2023

stories.headline: Singer Oliver Tree among six killed in mid-air helicopter collision over Rio de Janeiro

key_facts.fact: On Sunday morning June 14, two helicopters collided in mid-air over Recreio dos Bandeirantes in the western zone of Rio de Janeiro and crashed, killing all six people aboard

American singer and director Oliver Tree, 32, known for hits 'Life Goes On' and 'Miss You' with Robin Schulz, was among the dead, along with Argentine YouTuber Gaspar Prim, Lucas Vignale, Lucas Brito Chaves and pilots Alexandre Souza and Charles Marsillac

One helicopter crashed in the parking lot of a car dealership on Avenida das Américas, igniting a fire that burned approximately 20 electric vehicles before being extinguished; an investigation is underway to determine the cause

Tree was in Brazil on his world tour for the 2026 album 'Love You Madly Hate You Badly,' had performed in São Paulo on June 6, and was next scheduled to play Lisbon on July 1; he had over 11 million monthly Spotify listeners and nearly 20 million social-media followers

organizations: Rio de Janeiro Military Fire Department

stories.headline: Madrid-based Orbio raises $21M Series A led by Dawn Capital to automate hiring and onboarding for frontline workers

key_facts.fact: Orbio announced a $21 million Series A on Monday, June 14, in a round led by Dawn Capital.
Orbio's customers already include Poke and YUM! Brands (owners of Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and KFC), which use the platform to onboard and manage frontline employees.
Orbio's AI agents — named Maria, Daniel and Claire — can interview candidates, assess fit, monitor employee output and conduct daily check-ins throughout an employee's work lifecycle.
At behavioral health provider The Stepping Stones Group, Orbio now runs the company's full US operation, with 20% more candidates making it through to hire.

The platform reaches deskless workers through WhatsApp and phone calls, with no corporate login or email required, and Orbio's agents have been trained on millions of frontline conversations in healthcare, hospitality and logistics.
Orbio has raised about $26-28 million to date from investors including Visionaries, 2100 Ventures, Plus Partners and Enzo Ventures, with founders previously having sold startups Cobee and Nucoro.

stories.headline: Japan's Rapidus signs MoU with UK Semiconductor Centre on 2nm manufacturing as Takaichi visits London

key_facts.fact: Rapidus Corporation announced on June 15, 2026, that it signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the UK Semiconductor Centre (UKSC) for future semiconductor manufacturing.
The MoU was signed during Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's June 14 visit to the UK, where she met UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to advance Japan-UK technology cooperation.
Rapidus is currently conducting pilot production with the aim of mass-producing cutting-edge 2nm logic semiconductors in Japan in 2027.
UKSC CEO Andy McLean said the agreement 'further strengthens the UK's relationship with Japan' and supports the UK Government's AI Hardware Plan.

stories.headline: Russia hits Ukraine with 681 missiles and drones overnight in one of war's largest combined strikes

key_facts.fact: On the night of June 15 (from 18:00 on June 14), Russia launched 681 air attack weapons against Ukraine — 70 missiles and 611 strike UAVs — in a massive combined strike that primarily targeted Kyiv, with Dnipro and Kharkiv also attacked

The missile mix included 6 3M22 Zircon anti-ship missiles, 34 Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles, and 30 Kh-101/Iskander-K cruise missiles, alongside 611 Shahed, Gerbera, Italmas, Banderol loitering munitions and Parodiya decoy drones

Air defense shot down or suppressed 632 of 681 targets — 50 missiles (including 5 Zircons) and 582 drones — but 20 ballistic missiles and 27 strike UAVs hit 42 locations, with debris from downed drones falling at 12 more

Kyiv suffered widespread damage across nearly all districts; a hit was recorded in Kremenchuk in the Poltava region, where State Emergency Service reported damage to energy and agricultural infrastructure
President Zelensky said Russia has used about 2,800 strike drones, nearly 3,000 guided bombs, and 140 missiles of various types against Ukraine in June alone

stories.headline: Samsung's Rainbow Robotics pilots RB-Y1 humanoid at Coupang warehouse in first commercial test

key_facts.fact: Rainbow Robotics, the robot subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, has placed its mobile dual-arm robot RB-Y1 inside a Coupang fulfillment center for a warehouse-work pilot.
Industry sources confirmed the deployment on June 14; a large order from Coupang is expected if the robot passes the trial.
RB-Y1 is not a walking humanoid but has two arms on a wheeled base; payload is about three kilograms per arm, suiting it for lighter picking and sorting rather than heavy lifting.

The Coupang test marks the RB-Y1's first reported step from research labs onto a live commercial floor; previously the robot was used mainly by universities and research centers, with factory trials at Samsung and Toyota.
Coupang is testing the robot to reduce labor costs and prevent violations of South Korea's Serious Accidents Punishment Act.
None of the three companies has confirmed the pilot publicly.

stories.headline: SK Hynix accelerates HBM4E samples to this month, shares surge 7% on Korean market

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is expediting HBM4E sample shipments to major customers by this month or next, ahead of its previously stated second-half delivery timeline.
Industry sources first revealed the acceleration on June 14 Eastern Time.

The 12-layer HBM4E product features 4.0 TB/s bandwidth per stack (a 38% increase over the previous generation) and 33% increased die capacity, using a 1c-nanometer DRAM core and TSMC's 3-nanometer process for the base die.
SK Hynix shares surged approximately 7% following the news, leading Korean stocks.
Samsung Electronics took the lead in HBM4E by delivering its first batch of 12-layer 48GB HBM4E samples on May 29, intensifying competition.
TrendForce forecasts HBM4E to constitute 40% of total HBM demand by 2027.

stories.headline: SWI Group acquires $500M stake in Genesis Digital Assets to repurpose 1.3 GW bitcoin sites for AI

key_facts.fact: Euronext Amsterdam-listed SWI Group announced on June 15, 2026, the acquisition of a significant shareholding in Genesis Digital Assets Limited (GDA) for $500 million.
GDA holds 1.3 GW of energized and approved grid connections across 15 facilities, including multiple hyperscaler-grade sites in Texas.
SWI Group intends to reposition the platform from its current digital asset mining operations to high-performance computing and AI workloads, leveraging its AiOnX European data center platform.

Combined with AiOnX's 2.3 GW European platform across Ireland, the UK, Denmark, Spain, and Italy, the acquisition gives SWI Group a combined transatlantic footprint of 3.6 GW of AI-ready digital infrastructure capacity.

SWI Group CEO Max-Hervé George said: 'Power connectivity is the most valuable commodity in digital infrastructure today, and converting legacy cryptocurrency mining infrastructure to AI and high-performance computing is the best and highest use of these assets.'

stories.headline: Trump threatens 100% tariff on French wine and champagne unless Macron scraps 3% digital services tax

key_facts.fact: In an interview with the New York Post published June 15, Trump said he warned French President Emmanuel Macron directly: 'I asked him not to charge American companies, and if they do, I have no choice but to charge a 100% tariff on all champagnes and all wines coming out of France'

France's digital services tax, known as the GAFAM tax, has been in place since 2019 and levies a 3% charge on local revenues of large tech companies including Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Apple — generating about $700M for France last year, according to the French finance ministry

The US is the destination for about a fifth of France's wine industry global sales, worth over $2 billion annually; French and European wines exported to the US already face a 15% tariff, up from an earlier 10%

France's National Assembly in October voted 296-58 to double the digital tax to 6% and narrow the threshold to exclusively target the largest global players, though the measure was vetoed by ministers; Canada scrapped its own digital services tax last year under Trump pressure
The threat sets up a flashpoint at the G7 summit underway in Evian-les-Bains, France, which runs from June 15 to 17

stories.headline: UK to ban social media for under-16s, going further than Australia with livestream and chatbot restrictions

key_facts.fact: On June 15, Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced the UK will ban access to social media platforms for all children under 16, with the government hoping to pass regulation before Christmas and the ban coming into force by spring 2027

The ban will include Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook and X, and will block harmful functions such as livestreaming and stranger communication with under-16s on a wider range of online services including gaming sites; WhatsApp and Signal are not in scope

The government will use 'highly effective age assurance' (HEAA) measures and asked Ofcom for an urgent review of capabilities, citing Australia's experience where three in five 12- to 15-year-olds have managed to bypass restrictions

The announcement followed a public consultation that received over 116,000 responses; the government is also considering overnight curfews and breaks in infinite scrolling for under-18s, with more detail to follow in July

Starmer cited Grok, the AI feature on X, as a reason for tougher rules: 'When Grok (the AI feature of the social media platform X) started making nudes of children, women and celebrities without their consent, we challenged X and they backed down'

organizations: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

stories.headline: UK Royal Marines seize Russian shadow fleet tanker Smyrtos in English Channel, first such operation

key_facts.fact: In the early hours of June 14, Royal Marine Commandos and UK National Crime Agency officers boarded the oil tanker Smyrtos in the English Channel in a six-hour operation — the first UK boarding of a Russian shadow fleet vessel since authorization was granted in March

The Smyrtos was sailing under a Cameroon flag, having departed Russia's Baltic port of Ust-Luga on June 5 bound for Port Said, Egypt; the operation was supported by Chinook, Merlin Mk4 and Wildcat helicopters, an RAF Poseidon P-8A maritime patrol aircraft, the Type 23 frigate HMS Sutherland and Hunt-class minehunter HMS Ledbury, with French coordination

A 38-year-old Indian national was arrested on suspicion of sanctions offences under the Russia Regulations; the vessel will be held off the south coast of England near Weymouth for environmental and safety monitoring

The UK has sanctioned almost 600 shadow fleet vessels to date; Russia's oil revenues are down 27% from October 2024 levels and at their lowest point since the start of the war, according to the Ministry of Defence
Russian shadow fleet vessels had previously entered UK waters more than 200 times since the boarding authorization in March without being detained, until this first seizure

stories.headline: US and Iran reach deal to end war, reopen Strait of Hormuz; signing set for June 19 in Switzerland

key_facts.fact: On June 14, Trump posted on Truth Social that 'the Deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete' and authorized the immediate end of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, with the official signing scheduled for Friday June 19 in Switzerland

Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed the agreement on state television but said Iran would not start implementing it until signing; the deal followed over 14 hours of talks in Tehran with a representative from Qatar, with Pakistan as the other mediator

The agreement is a 14-point memorandum of understanding that codifies the ceasefires in Iran and Lebanon and outlines areas for future negotiation; broader talks on Iran's nuclear program would continue over the next 60 days, with the timeline extendable

The war began February 28 when the US and Israel struck Iran, killing supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei; Iran subsequently attacked Israel and Arab Gulf nations with missiles and drones, and a tenuous ceasefire was reached April 7 before the US imposed its naval blockade ten days later

The Strait of Hormuz normally handles about 20% of the world's oil and LNG supplies; the UK and France are preparing to help clear mines Iran is believed to have placed in the strait, with diplomats targeting normal shipment levels within about a month
